buggy_html:
Projects

Manage your active projects below.

Delete Project

Are you sure you want to permanently delete "Summer Campaign 2025"? This action cannot be undone and all associated data will be lost.
spec: The delete confirmation dialog must be accessible to screen reader users. When the dialog is open, screen readers must announce the dialog role and title automatically. The dialog must be identified with appropriate ARIA semantics. All interactive elements inside must have descriptive accessible names.
severity_reason: The modal has no role='dialog' and no aria-labelledby. Screen readers do not recognise it as a dialog and do not announce its title or purpose when it opens. Screen reader users navigating with the virtual cursor may browse the background page content instead of the dialog, not realising a confirmation is required.
red_herrings: The overlay background using rgba — this is a valid visual design choice, not a bug
The destructive action button using red colour — appropriate for a delete action and passes contrast requirements

model_report.title: Modal dialog missing role='dialog' and aria-labelledby — unrecognised by screen readers
model_report.steps:
1. Open the page
2. Inspect the HTML of the modal overlay element
3. Check for role='dialog', aria-modal, and aria-labelledby attributes
4. Check the close button for an accessible name
5. Test with a screen reader: does it announce 'dialog' when the overlay appears?
model_report.expected: The modal element has role='dialog' (or role='alertdialog'), aria-modal='true', and aria-labelledby pointing to the 'Delete Project' heading. The close button has aria-label='Close dialog'. Screen readers announce 'Delete Project dialog' when the overlay opens.
model_report.actual:
Bug 1 [CRITICAL]: The modal <div class='modal'> has no role='dialog'. Screen readers do not treat it as a dialog and may not announce it to the user when it appears.

Bug 2 [CRITICAL]: No aria-labelledby attribute — screen readers cannot associate the 'Delete Project' heading with the dialog, so the dialog's purpose is never announced.

Bug 3 [MAJOR]: No aria-modal='true' — the virtual cursor of screen readers can escape the overlay and browse the background page, making users unaware they need to respond to a confirmation.

Bug 4 [MAJOR]: The close button shows ✕ with no aria-label. Screen readers announce 'button' with no indication of its action.
